subject: general
question: In which of the following years was the Right to Information Act passed?
solution:
The correct answer is __**2005**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Right to Information Act** was passed by the Parliament of India in the year **2005**. It became effective on **12th October 2005**.
 
• This act empowers the citizens of India to seek information from public authorities, thus promoting transparency and accountability in governance. *Hence, the correct option is 2005.*
 
• The RTI Act covers all levels of government—**central, state, and local**. It mandates that public authorities must provide information within **30 days** of receiving a request.
 
• The act also recognizes the **right to access information as a fundamental right**, which is linked to **Article 19(1)(a)** of the Constitution of India, guaranteeing the freedom of speech and expression.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is 2005.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Right to Information Act, 2005:**

 
 
• The **RTI Act** was enacted to enhance accountability and transparency in government operations. It allows citizens to obtain information from public authorities, improving governance and reducing corruption.
 
• Under this act, any citizen can file an **RTI application** to seek information. The public authority is obligated to reply within **30 days**. In cases of life or liberty concerns, the information must be provided within **48 hours**.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of RTI Act:**
 
 
• **Coverage:** It applies to all constitutional authorities, including the executive, legislature, and judiciary, as well as bodies owned, controlled, or substantially financed by the government.
 
• **Exemptions:** Certain information is exempt under the act, such as matters affecting national security, trade secrets, and personal information that may invade privacy.
 
• **Public Information Officers (PIOs):** Each public authority is required to designate PIOs to handle requests and provide information under this act.
 
 
 
• **Impact of RTI:**
 
 
• The RTI Act has strengthened democracy by empowering citizens to question government actions and decisions.
 
• It has played a significant role in combating **corruption** by exposing irregularities and ensuring accountability.
 
• Several landmark RTI cases have led to policy changes and increased transparency in public services.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Legal Provisions:**

 
 
• The act includes provisions for **appeals** if information is denied. Citizens can approach the Central Information Commission or State Information Commission.
 
• RTI empowers citizens to hold public authorities accountable. However, misuse of RTI can lead to frivolous applications, which sometimes burden the system.
 
 
 
• **Examples of RTI Success Stories:**
 
 
• An RTI query in **2008** revealed the details of funds allocated under the Member of Parliament Local Area Development Scheme (MPLADS), exposing misuse.
 
• RTI was instrumental in uncovering irregularities in the **Commonwealth Games** held in India in **2010**.
 
• Information sought under RTI has been used to challenge unlawful practices and ensure justice in various cases.
